historical_reviews.deepseek: Incorrectly replaces the state-changing upgrade/reboot with a credentialed read-only query and says no risk.

original_test_intent: Install the authoritative NVIDIA Linux driver target, reboot, and prove the correct module version initializes every intended GPU without kernel, PCIe or service regression.
original_method: Inventory OS/kernel/architecture, current driver/package ownership, Secure Boot, GPUs/jobs and CUDA consumers; select signed exact target and vendor-supported install path; stage headers/rollback and console/OOB; preserve logs/drain jobs; install under approval; reboot once; verify module/file/package version, GPU UUID/BDF/count/model, nvidia-smi, applications/services and log deltas; rollback only by approved plan.
manual_activity: Driver owner resolves target/package method and rollback; operator drains workloads and controls maintenance/reboot/console; agent may install only the approved artifact and collect evidence.
required_inputs: Exact approved driver branch/version resolving R525/latest/R470
Existing package/runfile ownership, Secure Boot/module signing and DKMS policy
Compiler/kernel headers and approved installer options
Known-good driver/kernel rollback plus console/OOB and maintenance approval
safety_requirements: Never execute the literal R470 runfile while R525/latest conflict remains
Do not mix package-manager and runfile ownership without migration plan
Drain all GPU jobs and preserve logs before module replacement
No reboot without verified console/OOB and rollback
Stop on signature/build/module/GPU mismatch and never auto-retry
agent_execution_scope: Capture baseline and perform approved installation
Coordinate one reboot and collect complete module/GPU/service health
engineer_actions: Resolve target and approve install/rollback policy
Authorize service interruption and own recovery

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Credentialed `nvidia-smi` only checks current state and cannot cover source driver install/reboot; literal 470.57.02 is unsafe until target conflict is resolved.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the vendor-supported command for the signed approved target/package ownership model, capture install/module build logs, reboot under maintenance and verify `/proc/driver/nvidia/version` plus full `nvidia-smi` and health.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Upgrade, reboot and both version checks remain; R525/latest/R470 selection is not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a before/after transaction manifest covering package ownership, module signature/build, reboot, per-GPU identity/version and application/log health with a tested rollback entrypoint.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Eliminates ambiguous version selection and prevents a read-only check from masquerading as an upgrade.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Toolkit or nvidia-smi-only evidence cannot prove driver replacement and post-reboot initialization.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A failed module build/signature can strand all GPUs or host graphics/compute; console rollback must be available before installation.

project_override_considerations: Driver owner defines supported branch for the GPU/OS/CUDA recipe and whether repository packages or vendor runfile are authoritative.
expected_evidence: Approved target/package hash/signature and compatibility manifest
Pre/post OS/kernel/package/module ownership and Secure Boot state
Reboot/console timestamps and loaded module version
Per-GPU UUID/BDF/count/model and complete nvidia-smi plus CUDA/application health
dmesg/XID/AER/BMC/SEL deltas, rollback status and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Item requires R525, Procedure says latest, and the literal installer is R470 470.57.02; these are mutually incompatible target definitions.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Static review is complete; execution awaits an authoritative driver decision, package and approvals.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row283 Wistron-NV GPU-00276-V002: select one authoritative driver target among R525, latest and 470.57.02; approve signed package/hash, repository-versus-runfile ownership, OS/kernel/GPU/CUDA compatibility, Secure Boot/DKMS/install options, reboot and known-good rollback/OOB recovery.

review_improvement: Restores the actual state-changing driver transaction and makes target, module ownership, reboot initialization and rollback auditable.
independent_technical_reasoning: Driver branch affects kernel ABI, supported GPUs and CUDA compatibility. Mixing an older runfile with distribution packages can leave conflicting libraries/modules, while `nvidia-smi` may still show the pre-existing driver if installation never occurred. Post-reboot module identity, per-GPU enumeration and application/log health are required to prove the intended upgrade rather than a read-only snapshot.
